http://www.euronews.com/2026/09/02/tyler.text: The murder case against the Utah man accused of killing Charlie Kirk last year, Tyler Robinson, is headed for trial, and the defendant could face the death penalty if he’s convicted, according to a new court ruling.Utah District Judge Tony Graf sided with prosecutors on Tuesday who said they had “a mountain of evidence” that defendant Tyler Robinson fatally shot the conservative activist as he spoke to a crowd of thousands of students at Utah Valley University last September.Robinson pleaded not guilty to all counts, included aggravated murder, following Graf’s decision. The 23-year-old defendant turned himself in a day after the shooting, and his lawyers have not offered alternative theories for Kirk’s death.The defence team tried to block a trial or at least take the death penalty off the table, arguing that prosecutors failed to show Kirk’s shooting placed others around him at risk of death. That’s an aggravating factor under state law that makes Robinson eligible for capital punishment.Kirk's family called the ruling “an important step in our family’s pursuit of justice.”“Every step in this process carries the weight of all that Charlie’s murder has taken from his family, especially his children who will grow up without their father,” they said in a statement.Prosecutors said Robinson shot Kirk from a rooftop more than 122 meters away, knowing he could have missed and killed others at the open-air event.“Tyler James Robinson shot and killed Charlie Kirk because he disagreed with him, and he did it by firing a high-powered rifle into a crowd of over 3,000 people, which created a great risk of death that anyone would know about,” said Ryan McBride, a prosecutor with the Utah County Attorney’s Office.Graf had the option to send the case to trial on a lesser charge of murder, which carries a minimum sentence of 15 years and a maximum of life in prison. He said his decision to approve the aggravated murder charge was based on the positions of several people in and around a tent where Kirk was speaking, among other factors.Staci Visser, an attorney for Robinson, argued that prosecutors were trying to “shoehorn” the case into Utah's aggravated murder statute.Prior case law requires prosecutors to show that there was a high probability — not merely a possibility — that other people could have been killed, she said.Kirk was seated on a stage in an elevated position, not immediately near anyone else, when he was shot once in the neck.“There is one shot. There is one bullet. There is one victim,” said Visser. “There is zero evidence that there was any action taken towards other people.”Prosecutor Chad Grunander noted that the alleged murder weapon — a bolt-action rifle — was loaded with additional rounds that had not been fired, saying Robinson “came prepared to shoot again.”The Tuesday hearing in state court came after prosecutors in July spent five days presenting evidence, including DNA and a handwritten note they allege Robinson left for his romantic partner that read, “I had the opportunity to take out Charlie Kirk, and I took it.”Kirk’s parents, Robert and Kathryn Kirk, entered the heavily secured courthouse arm in arm before the hearing in Provo. His widow, Erika Kirk, was seated beside them. The family stepped out briefly while a prosecutor described the shooting. Erika Kirk and her mother-in-law held each other in a long embrace while the judge read his ruling.Robinson also faces potential sentencing enhancements if prosecutors can show he targeted Kirk for his political beliefs. Kirk was renowned among youth conservatives nationwide for his open-mic debates, and is seen as one of the biggest reasons behind President Trump’s 2024 re-election.Prosecutors argued that a bullet found in the rifle, engraved with “Hey Fascist! CATCH!”, shows that Kirk was targeted for how the defendant perceived his politics. They have also alleged Robinson wrote “I had enough of his hatred. Some hate can’t be negotiated out,” in a text message about Kirk.

Beállítom Ha egy ország pénzt, energiát, szakembereket és hat évet tesz egy kifejezetten korrupció felkutatására létrehozott hivatalba, de ezalatt egyetlen jogerős ítélet sem születik, akkor az ilyen hivatalt fel kell oszlatni – többek között erről is beszélt Hamran István, a szlovák rendőrség korábbi vezetője a bumm.sk-nak adott interjújában – célozva ezzel a magyar Nemzeti Vagyonvisszaszerzési és Vagyonvédelmi Hivatalra (NVVH). Hamran István a magyar NVVH működéséről, elszámoltatásról és a magyar korrupciós helyzetről is beszélt a szlovákiai magyar lapnak. Hamran 2021 és 2023 között vezette a szlovák rendőrséget, amikor a hatóságok korábban érinthetetlennek tartott politikusok, rendőri vezetők, ügyészek és üzletemberek ügyeiben is nyomozni kezdtek. A volt országos rendőrfőkapitány jelenleg az SaS biztonságpolitikai szakértője és lehetséges belügyminiszter-jelöltje. Hamran arról beszélt, hogy eleve kissé pesszimista volt, amikor azt hallotta, hogy létrehoznak egy hivatalt, amely majd visszaszerzi a közbeszerzéseken és más konstrukciókon keresztül illegálisan kimentett vagyont. „Kíváncsian várom, hogyan tudják mindezt visszamenőleg átvilágítani, bizonyítani, majd a vagyont ténylegesen visszaszerezni. Mi Szlovákiában ezen az úton már végigmentünk, de egyáltalán nem volt sétagalopp.” Viszont ami pozitív, hogy Magyarországon szerinte politikailag egyszerűbb a helyzet: egyszínű, kétharmados kormánytöbbség van, és amiben megegyeznek, azt végre is tudják hajtani. „Az NVVH ráadásul nagyon erős hatóság lett, külön költségvetéssel, állománnyal és széles jogkörökkel. Papíron tehát jók a feltételek.” A hivatal élére Unger Annát választották , ami a szlovák rendőrség exvezetőjét meglepte, mivel Unger politológus, nem dolgozott nyomozóként, ügyészként vagy bíróként, tehát büntetőeljárási gyakorlata nincs. Inkább elméleti és szervezési szakembernek tartja, ettől még az esélyt szerinte mindenkinek meg kell adni. Azzal viszont nem ért egyet, hogy Unger Anna azt mondta: szerinte botorság hat éven belül jogerős ítéletekre számítani. „Értem én, hogy a magyar bíróságok lassan dolgoznak, de ilyet az új hivatal vezetőjeként akkor sem lehet előre kijelenteni. Elveszi azok kedvét, akik elszámoltatást várnak.” Elmondta, hogy Szlovákiában a bíróságok nem voltak gyorsabbak, mégis két év alatt több mint negyven, közel ötven ember ügyében született jogerős elmarasztalás. Szerinte hat évre előre eredménytelenséget hirdetni elfogadhatatlan. Hamran azt is mondta, hogy a választás előtt kapcsolatban volt a Tisza egy-két munkatársával. „Abban maradtunk, hogy ha rendeződnek a dolgaik, találkozunk, és megnézzük, miben tudunk együttműködni. Albania: opposition MPs disrupt parliament with smoke flares Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 29 October 2026 - 15:08 GMT+1 Opposition MPs disrupted a parliamentary session in Albania by brandishing smoke flares and displaying photographs of injured protesters. They accused police of using violence against demonstrators demanding Prime Minister Edi Rama's resignation. … More Albania's parliament descended into chaos again on Thursday as opposition Democratic Party MPs set off smoke flares , blocked the podium and displayed photographs of protesters allegedly injured by police. The disruption came during a vote on central bank legislation , which governing Socialist Party lawmakers continued despite the protests. Four opposition MPs were expelled from the chamber. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT The parliamentary protest follows repeated demonstrations in Albania calling for the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama . Opposition lawmakers accuse police of using excessive force against people taking part in the protests, although the allegations are not independently established by the images presented. By bringing photographs of injured demonstrators into parliament, Democratic Party MPs sought to draw attention to their accusations against the security forces. The unrest followed similar scenes on 22 October , when opposition MPs surrounded the Speaker's podium, displayed photographs of students allegedly beaten by police and threw objects at Speaker Niko Peleshi . Clashes between rival lawmakers then forced parliamentary guards to intervene as microphones were torn from desks and chairs overturned .
